data.cause: The firewall's WAN NIC (vtnet0) transmit path is wedged — repeated "vtnet0: watchdog timeout on queue 0" in dmesg, 48k output errors, ARP to the ISP gateway incomplete, and every WAN-bound packet fails with "No buffer space available" — so even though the cable modem re-registered and reports OPERATIONAL since ~02:28, no traffic leaves the firewall; reloading the WAN interface (DHCP) does not reset the stuck driver, which is why 4 reloads this outage did nothing and the watchdog hit its 12-reload/24h cap at 03:30.
evidence: dmesg -a shows repeated 'vtnet0: watchdog timeout on queue 0' alternating with link DOWN/UP cycles (the reloads), i.e. the TX queue stays stuck across interface reloads

ping -c 3 8.8.8.8 and ping -c 3 198.51.100.1 both fail with 'ping: sendto: No buffer space available' (ENOBUFS) — 100% loss even to the directly-connected ISP gateway, while LAN ping to 10.20.0.9 works fine (0% loss)
arp -a -n shows '? (198.51.100.1) at (incomplete)' — ARP never completes because frames aren't leaving the NIC
netstat -i shows vtnet0 with Oerrs=48211 output errors, while netstat -m shows mbufs are NOT exhausted (0 denied), so ENOBUFS comes from a full/stuck transmit queue, not memory pressure

/var/db/wan-watchdog/events.jsonl: outage_start 02:06, four reloads (02:30, 02:40, 02:55, 03:25) all rc=0 yet traffic never returned; decision at 03:30 was 'none' with reason 'reload_cap' (reloads_24h=12 of max 12)

/var/db/wan-watchdog/modem-events.jsonl and modem-metrics.jsonl: provider-side blip ('No Ranging Response received - T3 time-out' 02:01:44, modem rebooted 02:28:21) but modem uptime 5280s and cm_status OPERATIONAL by 03:30 — the ISP link itself is back up, so the remaining fault is on the firewall side
data.recommendation: Reboot the firewall (firewall_reboot) to reset the hung vtnet0 device — this is the only listed action that re-initializes the NIC. A wan_reload won't help: it only redoes DHCP without resetting the driver, which the four already-failed reloads in this outage demonstrate. The maintainer is away, so submit the approval request anyway; if they can't be reached, let it run under its fallback conditions since the network has been down ~95 minutes and the watchdog's reload budget is exhausted. Afterwards, consider having the watchdog escalate to a full host reboot once its reload cap for an outage is reached, since repeated reloads clearly cannot recover this failure mode.
data.detail: vtnet0 WAN NIC transmit queue hung (TX watchdog timeouts)
